diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, NOS, non-germinal-center B-cell (non-GCB) phenotype by the Hans algorithm (CD10-, BCL6+, MUM1+). Hans non-GCB is an immunohistochemical surrogate and is not the same as the molecular activated B-cell (ABC) subtype, which requires gene-expression profiling. CD5 and EBER negative.
stage: Lugano (Ann Arbor) stage III with B symptoms (recurrent fevers and drenching night sweats; 7 kg weight loss is about 8% of body weight) and bulky disease (11.0 cm retroperitoneal mass, >=10 cm). Nodal disease above and below the diaphragm (left cervical, mediastinal, retroperitoneal) plus splenic involvement; the spleen is lymphatic tissue, not an extranodal site, so it does not raise the stage. No extranodal organ involvement on PET-CT and the bone marrow is negative.
biology: Double-expressor lymphoma by IHC: MYC 50% (>=40%) and BCL2 80% (>=50%). Not double-hit: FISH shows no MYC, BCL2 or BCL6 rearrangement, so this is not high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements. Double-expressor status is prognostically adverse but does not by itself change first-line therapy. Ki-67 ~85%.
prognosis: IPI 3 of 5, high-intermediate risk: age >60 (62), LDH elevated (735 U/L, about 3x ULN) and stage III; ECOG 1 and zero extranodal sites do not score. CNS-IPI 3 of 6, intermediate risk of CNS relapse (about 3-4% at 2 years): the spleen does not count as an extranodal site and there is no kidney or adrenal involvement.
first_line_treatment: Curative-intent immunochemotherapy. Recommend Pola-R-CHP (polatuzumab vedotin, rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, prednisone) for 6 cycles every 21 days as the preferred regimen: IPI >=2 matches POLARIX eligibility, and the progression-free survival benefit was most notable in non-GCB/ABC disease. R-CHOP for 6 cycles is an acceptable alternative. Give full doses; he is 62 with ECOG 1 and normal organ function. DA-EPOCH-R is not indicated for double-expressor biology without MYC/BCL2 rearrangements. Start entecavir before the first rituximab dose (see pretreatment workup). Consider consolidative ISRT to the initially bulky retroperitoneal site only if it remains PET-positive at the end of treatment.
cns_risk: CNS-IPI 3, intermediate risk; no high-risk extranodal sites (kidney, adrenal, testis, breast, uterus) and no neurologic symptoms. Routine CNS prophylaxis is not indicated (neither high-dose methotrexate nor intrathecal therapy). Routine MRI brain or lumbar puncture is not indicated without neurologic symptoms; image and sample CSF promptly if new neurologic symptoms develop.
response_assessment: FDG PET-CT at the end of treatment (6-8 weeks after the last cycle), read with Lugano 2014 criteria and the Deauville 5-point scale; Deauville 1-3 is a complete metabolic response. Interim PET-CT after cycles 2-4 is optional and should not change therapy unless it shows progression. Biopsy residual Deauville 4-5 uptake before changing therapy when it would change management; a residual PET-positive initially bulky site without other disease can be treated with ISRT.
pretreatment_workup: Hepatitis B serology shows HBsAg nonreactive, anti-HBc total reactive and anti-HBs reactive: resolved (past) HBV infection, which carries a high risk of HBV reactivation with rituximab and other anti-CD20 antibodies even though HBsAg is negative. Send a quantitative HBV DNA and hepatic panel before cycle 1; if HBV DNA is detectable, manage as chronic HBV with hepatology input. Start entecavir 0.5 mg by mouth daily (tenofovir is an alternative) before the first rituximab dose, and continue it for at least 12 months after the last rituximab dose. Monitor ALT and HBV DNA every 1-3 months during therapy and after entecavir stops. HCV and HIV nonreactive. Echocardiogram LVEF 58%, adequate for anthracycline. PET-CT, bone marrow and FISH are complete.
supportive_care: Tumor lysis syndrome risk is at least intermediate (11 cm mass, LDH about 3x ULN, uric acid 6.8-7.1, normal renal function): allopurinol 300 mg daily starting 2-3 days before cycle 1, oral plus IV hydration, and TLS labs (potassium, phosphate, calcium, uric acid, creatinine, LDH) within 24-72 hours of cycle 1; escalate to rasburicase if uric acid rises or creatinine climbs. Primary G-CSF prophylaxis (pegfilgrastim) with each cycle is reasonable. Entecavir antiviral prophylaxis as above. Echocardiogram LVEF 58% permits anthracycline. Antiemetics per regimen. Levothyroxine, omeprazole and atorvastatin can continue. Counsel about alopecia and peripheral neuropathy with polatuzumab.
fitness_and_goals: Fit for full-dose curative-intent therapy: ECOG 1, age 62, normal renal and hepatic function, LVEF 58%, and well-controlled comorbidities (hypothyroidism, GERD, hyperlipidemia). His goal is cure and continuing part-time work; full-dose therapy is aligned with that goal. Six 21-day cycles starting late September would finish around January 2027, before his daughter's May wedding. Limit job-site travel during nadirs.
missing_information: Quantitative HBV DNA level (not yet sent; needed at baseline given reactive anti-HBc)
